# Available Scene Object Types

Use any value below as the `object_type` parameter in `add_builtin_object()`.

> When `Structure:` shows children / siblings / parent, those auto-created objects
> appear in the `_autoCreated` array of the add_builtin_object response —
> read GUIDs from there to address them.

## 3D Mesh (11)
- **3D Gaussian Splatting**: 3D Gaussian Splatting is an advanced AI-driven 3D rendering technology that uses Gaussian ellipsoids ('splats') to represent and render 3D scenes as an alternative to polygon-based meshes. Supports Splat and Point rendering modes with Spherical Harmonic lighting for realistic illumination.
  - Components: GSplatRenderer
- **3D Text**: 3D Text adds text to effects as a rendered element in the 3D scene. Supports most languages and multi-line content. Typical use cases include quiz/randomizer effects, karaoke lyrics, and input-driven text displays.
  - Components: Text2D
- **3D Text Mesh**: 3D Text Mesh adds text as a 3D mesh to effects, supporting 3D geometry rendering with depth and perspective. Uses the Text component with a Transform for placement in 3D space.
  - Components: Text3D
- **Basic Cloth**: Basic Cloth is a physics-based cloth simulation object for creating realistic fabric effects like flags, veils, and draped fabrics. Uses Cloth and Cloth Configuration components. Recommended vertex count: 100-500.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, ClothActor, ClothMaterial
- **Cube**: Cube is a 3D box primitive (8×8×8 world units at default scale) that can be moved, rotated, and scaled in 3D space. Apply textures, materials (e.g., Standard PBR), and post-process effects via the Mesh Renderer component to alter its appearance.
  - Structure: Cube[MeshRenderer] + sibling Directional Light[DirectionalLight], Environment Light[EnvironmentLighting]
- **Empty Mesh**: Empty Mesh is a 3D object with a Mesh Renderer component but no default mesh assigned. Use it as a starting point for custom 3D content by assigning your own imported mesh and material.
  - Structure: Empty Mesh[MeshRenderer] + sibling Directional Light[DirectionalLight], Environment Light[EnvironmentLighting]
- **Empty Object**: Empty Object is a container that does not render on its own. Use it to group and organize other 3D objects under a shared Transform, so child objects can be moved, rotated, and scaled together as a single unit.
  - Components: (none)
- **Head**: Head provides a 3D head mesh that can be used for face effects. It can be combined with face tracking to create head-fitting overlays and deformation effects.
  - Structure: Head[MeshRenderer] + sibling Directional Light[DirectionalLight], Environment Light[EnvironmentLighting]
- **Image**: Image is a 3D image plane that displays a texture in 3D world space. Unlike Screen Image which exists in 2D screen space, Image can be positioned, rotated, and scaled like any 3D object. Uses the Image component to directly assign a texture. WARNING: Image renders in the transparent queue with BOTH depth test and depth write disabled — overlap between two Images is resolved by draw order, not by the depth buffer, and an Image can be fully hidden behind another drawn later even when it is closer to the camera (typically when both transforms share the same world Z). For 2D-texture entities that must occlude each other correctly in a 3D scene (grounds, walls, standee characters), prefer Plane with a depth-tested material; reserve Image for isolated billboards that never overlap other world-space content.
  - Components: Image
- **Plane**: Plane is a flat 3D surface (8×8 world units, single-sided quad). By default the plane lies on the XY plane facing +Z (toward camera, vertical). To use as a ground/floor, set localEulerAngles to (-90, 0, 0) so the visible face points UP (+Y). WARNING: (90, 0, 0) makes the visible face point DOWN — invisible from above due to backface culling. At default scale (1,1,1) it spans 8×8 world units. Plane is the PREFERRED way to display a 2D texture in a 3D scene (pseudo-3D stages, standee characters, textured floors/walls): its opaque, depth-tested material makes occlusion follow world positions correctly, unlike the 3D Image object whose transparent-queue rendering ignores the depth buffer. Assign the texture through the material (e.g. Unlit with _AlbedoTexture); for transparent-background stickers enable alpha test (_EnableAlphaTest, _AlbedoCutoff).
  - Structure: Plane[MeshRenderer] + sibling Directional Light[DirectionalLight], Environment Light[EnvironmentLighting]
- **Sphere**: Sphere is a 3D sphere primitive (diameter 10 world units at default scale) that can be moved, rotated, and scaled in 3D space. Apply textures and materials via the Mesh Renderer component to alter its appearance.
  - Structure: Sphere[MeshRenderer] + sibling Directional Light[DirectionalLight], Environment Light[EnvironmentLighting]

## 2D Object (5)
- **2D Mask**: 2D Mask constrains the visible area of its child objects — any Screen Image, 2D Text, or texture placed as a child is clipped to the mask's defined region. Use it to create focused visuals, reveal effects, or control content visibility within a defined screen area.
  - Components: Mask
- **2D Scene Object**: 2D Scene Object is an invisible empty container for grouping other 2D objects under a shared Screen Transform. Child 2D objects can be manipulated together as a single unit. The 2D equivalent of the Empty Object. Automatically nested under a 2D Camera.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → 2D Scene Object
- **2D Text**: 2D Text displays rich, customizable text in 2D screen space. Its Text component exposes set_component-settable text, fontSize, bold, italic, underline, color, and writingDirection. Rich styling (gradient/texture fills, layered body/stroke/shadow/background, outlines, glow, and bend) is configured via an ArtTextAsset assigned to the Text component's `artText` property — not by setting individual properties. Alignment (horizontalAlignment/verticalAlignment) is settable like any other property, using the schema's enum values (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT/JUSTIFY and TOP/CENTER/BOTTOM).
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → 2D Text[Text2D]
- **Screen Drawing**: Screen Drawing provides a 2D drawing canvas that responds to touch input, allowing users to draw on the screen by touching it. When added, it automatically sets up a 2D Camera and a Draw on Touch interaction in Visual Scripting.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Screen Drawing[Image]
- **Screen Image**: Screen Image creates a 2D image displayed in screen space (flat, non-perspective). When added, it automatically creates a companion 2D Camera (Orthographic) required to render 2D content. Supports importing PNG or JPG textures for backgrounds, UI elements, and overlays. SOLID-COLOR RECTANGLE: an Image with no texture renders as a gray placeholder, so do NOT generate/import an image just to get a colored panel — instead point the Image component's `texture` at the built-in white texture (a resource that already exists, no creation needed: set texture to { guid: "r26" }, the built-in White_Texture.png) and set `color` to tint it. The white texture multiplies with `color`, yielding a crisp solid-color fill; adjust `opacity` for transparency.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Screen Image[Image]

## Camera & Light (6)
- **Camera**: Camera is used to display the objects in your scene. Every effect requires at least one Camera. Supports Perspective mode (3D, default) for depth and volume, and Orthographic mode (2D, flattened) for screen-space rendering. Controls layer-based rendering, render order, and output to custom Render Textures.
  - Components: Camera
- **Directional Light**: Directional Light emits even, uniform light from a single direction, simulating sunlight or any scene where all objects receive equal illumination. A light's layer assignment applies across all render groups.
  - Components: DirectionalLight
- **Environment Light**: Environment Light provides global ambient and environment lighting to enhance the overall illumination of 3D content. Included in every new Effect House project by default. Uses an environment map texture for image-based lighting.
  - Components: EnvironmentLighting
- **Point Light**: Point Light emits light equally in all directions from a single point and gets dimmer the farther away the light is, simulating a lamp or light bulb.
  - Components: PointLight
- **Smart Camera**: Smart Camera provides AI-driven camera movement effects using the CineMove component, creating cinematic camera motions with preset modes for dynamic video capture.
  - Components: Camera, CineMove
- **Spot Light**: Spot Light emits cone-shaped light from a single point, fading with distance, like a flashlight, stage spotlight, or beam through a window. Useful for focused highlighting of specific objects.
  - Components: SpotLight

## Particle & Animation (12)
- **Audio Player**: Audio Player allows you to import and play MP3 audio files in your effect. Supports configurable volume, play mode (single or looped with loop count), autoplay, and mute. Can be exposed as a Visual Scripting node for dynamic control of play/stop/pause/resume.
  - Components: AudioComponent
- **Basic Particles**: Basic Particles creates a GPU particle system using the Visual Effects Editor's node-based graph (Spawn-Init-Update-Output). Supports various spawn modes, flipbook animation, turbulence, collision, GPU events, and visual scripting integration.
  - Components: VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Physics Particles**: Physics Particles creates a physics-enabled particle system where particles interact with gravity, collisions, and forces. Built on the same Visual Effects Editor as Basic Particles with additional physics simulation capabilities.
  - Components: VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Timeline**: Timeline provides sequential animation and event control for effects using the Timeline Editor. Supports keyframe-based animation of object properties (position, rotation, scale, visibility) along with Video, Audio, and TikTok Sounds tracks.
  - Components: TimelinePlayer, Animator
- **Explosion Particles**: White dot particles burst radially outward from center, expanding to cover most of the screen, then fade out within ~1 second. Auto-loops continuously. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Fire Particles**: Orange-yellow flame-textured particles rise upward from origin. Default size ~1/4 screen width, ~1/5 screen height. Continuously emitting with built-in flame textures. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Firework Particles**: Firework rockets launch upward from bottom, burst into colorful sparks (white, yellow, cyan, pink) at top. Covers most of screen when bursting. Auto-loops. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Fog Particles**: Gray-white semi-transparent cloud/smoke particles slowly expand from center. Default ~1/4 screen coverage. Soft diffuse appearance with built-in cloud textures. Continuously emitting. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Lightning Particles**: Blue-white electric lightning bolt streaks downward from center with branching forks. Spans ~half screen height. Bright glow with built-in lightning textures. Continuously animating. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Rain Particles**: Thin white vertical streaks fall rapidly from top. Sparse density, covers full screen width. Narrow elongated streaks simulating rain. Continuously emitting. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Snow Particles**: White round snowflake particles of varying sizes drift downward from top. Full screen width, moderate density. Gently floating motion. Continuously emitting. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController
- **Turbulence Particles**: Blue-white glowing round particles swirl chaotically around origin. ~1/3 screen coverage. Turbulent non-linear paths. Continuously emitting. APJS: play()/stop()/emit().
  - Components: Transform, VFXEffectBlock, VFXEffectBlockController

## Segmentation (17)
- **Building Segmentation**: Building Segmentation isolates buildings and architectural structures in the camera view, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied. Useful for building color effects and architectural AR overlays.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Building Segmentation[Image]
- **Clothing Segmentation**: Clothing Segmentation isolates the subject's clothing, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied to the clothes region. Useful for virtual clothing try-on effects and fabric texture overlays.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Clothing Segmentation[Image]
- **Ear Segmentation**: Ear Segmentation isolates the subject's ear regions, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied to the ears. Useful for ear decoration effects and earring highlights.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Ear Segmentation[Image]
- **Eye Segmentation**: Eye Segmentation isolates the subject's eye regions, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied to the eyes. Useful for eye color effects, eye glitter, and glow overlays.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Eye Segmentation[Image]
- **Face Segmentation**: Face Segmentation isolates the subject's face region as a 2D image mask, allowing custom textures to be applied exclusively to the face area. Not needed for face-tracking 3D effects (Face Mask, Eye Color, Face Stretch, etc.) which have their own built-in tracking.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Face Segmentation[Image]
- **Face Sticker**: Face Sticker Segmentation isolates a portion of the face and applies a custom texture or effect as a sticker overlay on that region. More targeted than Portrait Segmentation, designed for sticker-like face overlays and regional face decorations.
  - Structure: Face Sticker[FaceBindingV2JS] → Image[Image] + sibling Portrait[Image]
- **Ground Segmentation**: Ground Segmentation isolates the ground or floor surface in the camera view, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied. Useful for floor texture replacement and ground glow effects.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Ground Segmentation[Image]
- **Hair Segmentation**: Hair Segmentation isolates the subject's hair, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied exclusively to the hair region. Useful for hair color filters, sparkle overlays, and dye effects.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Hair Segmentation[Image]
- **Hand Segmentation**: Hand Segmentation isolates the subject's hands, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied to the hand region. Useful for hand color effects, glove overlays, and shadow effects.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Hand Segmentation[Image]
- **Head Segmentation**: Head Segmentation isolates the subject's entire head silhouette, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied to the head region. Provides wider coverage than Hair Segmentation, covering the full head outline.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Head Segmentation[Image]
- **Lip Segmentation**: Lip Segmentation isolates the subject's lip region, allowing custom textures and colors to be applied precisely to the lips. Useful for lipstick try-on, lip glitter, and animated lip effects.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Lip Segmentation[Image]
- **Pet Segmentation**: Pet Segmentation detects and isolates pets in the camera frame, separating them from the background for applying customized textures and effects to the pet or background layer.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Pet Segmentation → Background[Image], Pet[Image]
- **Portrait Segmentation**: Remove background. Background removal: erase or replace the background behind a person. Detects the person in the camera feed and separates them from the background. Creates a Portrait object (just the person) and a Background object under a 2D Camera, each styleable independently.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Portrait Segmentation → Background[Image], Portrait[Image]
- **Skin Segmentation**: Skin Segmentation isolates the subject's exposed skin regions, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied exclusively to the skin areas. Useful for body paint, skin texture overlays, and skin color filter effects.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Skin Segmentation[Image]
- **Sky Segmentation**: Sky Segmentation isolates the sky region in the camera view, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied. Useful for sky replacement effects, sky color tinting, and cloud overlays.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Sky Segmentation[Image]
- **Subject Segmentation**: Subject Segmentation isolates the most prominent object on the screen, regardless of whether it is a person. Unlike Portrait Segmentation which targets people, Subject Segmentation can isolate any visually prominent object such as a product or pet.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Subject Segmentation[Image]
- **Teeth Segmentation**: Teeth Segmentation isolates the subject's visible teeth area, allowing custom textures and effects to be applied. Useful for teeth whitening, sparkle effects, and color overlays.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Teeth Segmentation[Image]

## AR Tracking (19)
- **2D Keypoint Tracker**: 2D Keypoint Tracker tracks 18 body keypoints (joints: wrists, elbows, knees, ankles, etc.) in 2D screen space in real time, enabling virtual items to be attached to specific body parts. Supports pose estimation and action recognition via visual scripting.
  - Components: BodyBindingJS
- **3D Hand Tracker**: 3D Hand Tracker provides precise 3D skeletal tracking for both left and right hands simultaneously, including per-finger joint keypoints. Creates both a Left Hand Tracker and Right Hand Tracker in the hierarchy for high-fidelity hand-driven AR effects.
  - Structure: 3D Hand Tracker[Hand3dAvatarDrive] + sibling havatar_hierarchy_hand_tracking_right_display[Hand3dAvatarDrive]
- **AR Brush**: AR Brush enables drawing in augmented reality by touching the screen with your finger. Works with the AR Camera in world tracking mode for interactive real-time AR drawing experiences.
  - Structure: AR Brush[ARBrush] + sibling Camera[Camera]
- **AR Ceiling**: AR Ceiling tracks ceiling surfaces for placing 3D content in augmented reality, complementing AR Plane which tracks floor and table surfaces.
  - Structure: AR Ceiling[MeshRenderer] + sibling AR Camera[Camera, DeviceTracker]
- **AR Plane**: AR Plane detects real-world flat surfaces (floors, tables) using the device camera and allows 3D models to be placed and anchored on those surfaces. Automatically adds an AR Camera with Device Tracker in World tracking mode.
  - Structure: AR Plane[MeshRenderer] + sibling AR Camera[Camera, DeviceTracker]
- **Body Avatar Drive**: Body Avatar Drive maps real-time body keypoints detected by the camera onto the joints of a custom 3D character model, driving full-body character animation from the user's movements. Requires a properly rigged 3D character with correctly named joints.
  - Components: FullBodyAvatar
- **Body Brush**: Body Brush enhances AR drawing by tracking fingertip positions in 3D space via the camera, allowing users to draw in the air using pinch gestures without screen contact. Supports customizable brush texture, color, size, and rainbow mode.
  - Structure: Body Brush[Camera] + sibling Camera[Camera]
- **Cat Face Reshape**: Cat Face Reshape adjusts a cat's facial features using a brush tool in the Scene panel, providing fine-grained control over cat facial geometry.
  - Components: CatFaceWarpXComponent
- **Cat Face Stretch**: Cat Face Stretch deforms a cat's facial proportions by moving key points on a 2D cat face template, producing stretched or exaggerated cat face effects. Works the same as Face Stretch but with cat-specific landmarks.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, CatFaceStretchComponent, FaceStretchController
- **Dog Face Reshape**: Dog Face Reshape adjusts a dog's facial features using a brush tool in the Scene panel, providing fine-grained control over dog facial geometry.
  - Components: DogFaceWarpXComponent
- **Dog Face Stretch**: Dog Face Stretch deforms a dog's facial proportions by moving key points on a 2D dog face template, producing stretched or exaggerated dog face effects. Works the same as Face Stretch but with dog-specific landmarks.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, DogFaceStretchComponent, FaceStretchController
- **Fingernail Tracker**: Fingernail Tracker tracks all five fingernails individually, enabling virtual nail art (custom colors, images, textures) to be applied and precisely fit to each nail in real time. Creates five separate child objects for each fingernail.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Fingernail Tracker → Thumbnail[Nail], Index Fingernail[Nail], Middle Fingernail[Nail], Ring Fingernail[Nail], Pinky Fingernail[Nail]
- **Hand Tracker**: Hand Tracker tracks one hand visible in the camera view, allowing 3D objects, special effects, or interaction triggers to be attached to it. Add multiple Hand Tracker objects to track more than one hand.
  - Components: HandCapture
- **Head Collider**: Head Collider enables collision detection for objects attached to or near the user's head, allowing physics-based interactions between head-tracked objects and other scene objects.
  - Structure: Face Binding[FaceBindingV2JS] → Head Collider[MeshRenderer, SphereCollider, CapsuleCollider, SphereCollider, CapsuleCollider]
- **Head Tracker**: Head Tracker creates a Face Binding > Head two-level hierarchy. The Face Binding parent has a Face Binding component anchored to FaceCenter. The Head child has a Mesh Renderer with a head occluder mesh. Head bounds are approximately 18x29x21 world units. To add AR face decorations, parent 3D objects (Cube, Sphere, etc.) to the Head child object — they will automatically follow face movement. Supports up to 5 simultaneous faces.
  - Structure: Face Binding[FaceBindingV2JS] → Head Tracker[MeshRenderer]
- **Neck Tracker**: Neck Tracker simulates neck tracking using 5 weighted bones driven by the head-tracking algorithm, allowing objects like necklaces, collars, or shoulder-attached accessories to follow head and neck movements naturally.
  - Components: HeadNeckTracker
- **Pet Face Sticker**: Pet Face Sticker anchors a 2D image or animated texture to a detected pet's face at specific facial landmark points, following the pet's face in real time.
  - Structure: Pet Face Sticker[PetFaceCapture] → Pet Face Sticker[Image]
- **Pet Head Tracker**: Pet Head Tracker uses face detection to track a pet's head in real time, allowing 2D images or 3D models to be attached as child objects that follow the pet's head movement.
  - Structure: Pet Head Tracker[PetFaceCapture] → Pet Head Tracker[MeshRenderer]
- **Target Tracker**: Target Tracker detects a user-uploaded reference image in the real world and places a designated AR object at the detected location in real time. Best results with high-contrast, non-repeating, sharp target images. Recommended maximum 3 per effect.
  - Structure: Target Tracker[TargetTrackingJS] → Cube[MeshRenderer] + sibling AR Camera[Camera, TargetTrackingCameraJS]

## Face & Beauty (19)
- **3D Eye**: 3D Eye adds animated 3D eye meshes that track and replace or overlay the user's eyes, enabling stylized or supernatural eye effects. Includes a customizable Eye Material with iris, pupil, sclera, and catchlight properties.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, Eye3D
- **3D Eyelashes**: 3D Eyelashes places a 3D eyelash mesh on the user's eyes with configurable style, length, curl, density, and color, enabling realistic or colorful volumized lash effects.
  - Structure: 3D Eyelashes[FaceBindingV2JS] → 3D Eyelashes[Eyelashes3D]
- **3D Face Binding Mesh**: 3D Face Binding Mesh provides a 3D mesh mask that conforms to the user's face in real time, enabling 3D face paint, face swap effects, and morph-based deformations. Requires a custom 3D mesh exported from the provided face template.
  - Structure: 3D Face[FaceBindingV2JS] → 3D Face Binding Mesh[MeshRenderer]
- **3D Face Warp**: 3D Face Warp applies 3D mesh-based face deformation with 66 independently adjustable parameters for warping head shape, eyes, nose, mouth, jaw, and other facial features in real time. More precise and 3D-accurate than the 2D Face Stretch.
  - Components: FaceDistortion3D
- **3D Head Binding Mesh**: 3D Head Binding Mesh places a real-time 3D mesh mask over the user's entire head, enabling head deformation effects, head-fitting overlays, or custom 3D head models. Can be combined with the Deformation component for morph-target-based shape animations.
  - Structure: 3D Head[FaceBindingV2JS] → 3D Head Binding Mesh[MeshRenderer]
- **3D Portrait Segmentation**: Remove background, extract the person as a movable 3D layer. Background removal with the isolated person repositionable in 3D space for parallax, echo, or spatial displacement. Uses an Unlit material; unlike standard Portrait Segmentation the extracted portrait is freely transformable in the scene.
  - Components: Image
- **Eye Color**: Eye Color applies a custom color or texture overlay to one or both eyes, enabling iris color changes, decorative eye designs, and colored contact lens effects. It is fully self-contained with built-in eye tracking — no Face Segmentation or other segmentation object is needed.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, EyeColorV2
- **Eye Effect**: Eye Effect is a preconfigured Face Mask with the face region set to Eyes, used to apply eye shadow textures to the eye region. A reference eye model appears in the Scene panel while editing.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, FaceMask
- **Eyelash Effect**: Eyelash Effect is a preconfigured Face Mask targeting the eyelash region, used to apply custom eyelash texture overlays for virtual mascara or decorative lash effects.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, FaceMask
- **Face Fusion**: Face Fusion blends the user's live face with a target photo texture, morphing their face into another person's face or character over a configurable duration (0-10 seconds). Supports skin tone matching to blend the fused texture naturally.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Face Fusion[Image]
- **Face Inset**: Face Inset cuts out a selected region of the face (eyes, nose, mouth, eyebrows, or full face) as a standalone 2D element that can be freely repositioned in the scene. Always comes with a Face Binding child object to control face tracking.
  - Structure: Face Binding[FaceBindingV2JS] → Face Inset[FaceInsetV2Component]
- **Face Mask**: Face Mask applies a 2D texture overlay directly onto the user's face to create face paint, makeup, or cosmetic effects. The texture is mapped to facial landmarks and follows the face in real time. Supports region selection (Whole face, Eyes, Eyelashes, Lips, Teeth) and multi-face targeting.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, FaceMask
- **Face Reshape**: Face Reshape adjusts facial features using key points or brush tools in the Scene panel. Provides fine-grained control over facial geometry for reshaping specific areas of the face.
  - Components: FaceWarpXComponent
- **Face Retouch**: Face Retouch applies AI-powered facial retouching enhancements, including skin texture smoothing (pores/fine lines), eye brilliance boosting, dark circle reduction, and smile line softening. Supports multi-face targeting.
  - Components: SkinSmoothing
- **Face Stretch**: Face Stretch deforms facial proportions by letting creators drag key points on a 2D face template to warp and stretch specific facial features. Supports adjustable intensity, symmetric mode, and additive stacking of multiple Face Stretch objects.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, FaceStretchComponent
- **Lip Effect**: Lip Effect is a preconfigured Face Mask targeting the lip region, used to apply custom lip color or lipstick texture overlays that track the user's lips in real time.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, FaceMask
- **Liquify**: Liquify applies a real-time mesh warp to facial and body features by placing Liquify objects over key facial points, letting creators push, pull, or resize specific areas of the face for beauty or distortion effects.
  - Structure: Face Binding[FaceBindingV2JS] → Liquify[MeshRenderer, LiquifyComponent]
- **Outline**: Outline detects and draws a configurable contour line around a detected subject. Supports multiple subject types including Human, Pet, Hand, Clothing, Sky, Ground, Building, Skin, and Custom Depth, with customizable line type, brush style, color gradient, speed, and animation.
  - Components: FindContour
- **Teeth Whitening**: Teeth Whitening is a preconfigured Face Mask targeting the teeth region, applying a brightening or whitening color effect to the user's visible teeth.
  - Components: MeshRenderer, FaceMask

## Generative Effect (22)
- **Aged**: Aged is a generative effect that uses GANs (Generative Adversarial Networks) to digitally age the user's face, adding wrinkles, skin texture changes, and other aging markers. Includes a companion distortion object for face shape modification.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Big Smile**: Big Smile is a generative effect that uses GANs to create an exaggerated, wide smile expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Blonde Hair**: Blonde Hair is a generative effect that uses GANs to instantly transform the user's hair to blonde. The generation blends seamlessly to match the surrounding skin without requiring a separate segmentation object.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Cartoon**: Cartoon is a generative effect that uses GANs to transform the user's face into a cartoon style. Offers two selectable style types (Type 1 and Type 2) from the Inspector.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Eyebrow Eraser**: Eyebrow Eraser is a generative effect that uses GANs to digitally remove the user's eyebrows, creating a smooth appearance that blends with the surrounding skin.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Hair Color**: Hair Color applies real-time hair coloring effects to the user's detected hair. Supports four modes: Full (single solid color), Two Tone (split color), Streaks (up to 4 colors), and Custom Texture, with controls for opacity, coverage, and bleach intensity.
  - Components: DyeHairJS
- **Hair Eraser**: Hair Eraser is a generative effect that uses GANs to digitally remove the user's hair, creating a bald appearance that blends with the surrounding skin.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Hair Eraser(Partial)**: Hair Eraser (Partial) is a generative effect that uses GANs to partially remove the user's hair, creating a receding hairline appearance rather than complete removal.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Mouth Closed**: Mouth Closed is a generative effect that uses GANs to close the user's mouth in a natural-looking way.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Neutral**: Neutral is a generative effect that uses GANs to neutralize the user's facial expression, creating a calm, expressionless look.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **No Beard**: No Beard is a generative effect that uses GANs to digitally remove the user's beard and facial hair, creating a clean-shaven appearance that blends naturally.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Pout**: Pout is a generative effect that uses GANs to push out the user's lips into a pouting expression.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Pucker**: Pucker is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a puckered lip expression on the user's face, as if blowing a kiss.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Sad Face**: Sad Face is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a sad, downturned expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Shocked**: Shocked is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a shocked or surprised expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Side Eye**: Side Eye is a generative effect that uses GANs to move the user's eye gaze to the side, creating a side-eye look.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Slanted Smile**: Slanted Smile is a generative effect that uses GANs to create an asymmetric, lopsided smile expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Slow Blink**: Slow Blink is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a slow blinking animation on the user's eyes.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Smile**: Smile is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a natural smiling expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Thrilled**: Thrilled is a generative effect that uses GANs to create an excited, thrilled expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Wink**: Wink is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a winking expression on the user's face.
  - Components: GanComponent
- **Yell**: Yell is a generative effect that uses GANs to create a yelling or shouting expression on the user's face with an open mouth.
  - Components: GanComponent

## Filter & Post Effect (12)
- **AI Filter**: AI Filter is a post effect that uses AI-powered stylization to transform the visual output of the scene, applying intelligent image processing beyond traditional LUT-based color grading.
  - Components: AIFilter
- **Bling**: Bling is a post effect that creates sparkling, glittering overlay effects on the scene using animated sparkle textures. Supports up to three swappable sparkle textures with controls for opacity, brightness, intensity, size, speed, and color tints.
  - Components: Camera, BlingV2
- **Bloom**: Bloom is a Post Process effect that creates a glow-like illusion of bleeding light around bright areas in the scene, simulating the way camera lenses overexpose intense light sources.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Bokeh Blur**: Bokeh Blur is a Post Process effect that simulates depth-of-field camera blur, making objects outside the focal plane appear softly out-of-focus with characteristic circular bokeh shapes.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Chromatic Aberration**: Chromatic Aberration is a Post Process effect that simulates color fringing by splitting RGB channels apart at high-contrast edges, creating the look of a cheap or distorted lens.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Custom**: Custom is a Post Process effect that lets you apply a custom material as a full-screen post-processing shader pass, enabling arbitrary screen-space visual effects such as pixelation, custom distortions, or stylized looks.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Distort**: Distort is a Post Process effect that applies geometric distortion to the full screen, with controls for barrel/pincushion distortion, rotation, zoom, and dynamic wave distortion via configurable amplitude, frequency, and speed.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Filter**: Filter is a post effect that applies LUT (Lookup Table) based color grading to transform the entire camera output. Use it to create black-and-white, cinematic, vintage, or custom color-graded looks. Built-in LUT textures are available in the Asset Library, and custom LUTs can be created in Photoshop.
  - Components: FilterV2
- **Grain**: Grain is a Post Process effect that adds film-like noise (random pixels) to the screen, creating a textured, cinematic, or lo-fi look with configurable strength, color intensity, and animation speed.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Lens Flare**: Lens Flare is a Post Process effect that simulates the optical flare artifact caused by bright light sources hitting camera lens elements, producing streaks, halos, and circular highlights.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Motion Blur**: Motion Blur is a Post Process effect that creates a trailing blur based on object motion in the scene, simulating camera shutter motion blur for a sense of speed and dynamism.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess
- **Vignette**: Vignette is a Post Process effect that darkens the edges of the screen toward the corners while leaving the center brighter, drawing attention to the center of the frame.
  - Components: Camera, PostProcess

## Media & Social (12)
- **Friends Leaderboard**: Friends Leaderboard displays the built-in TikTok friends-ranking UI. Use it when the scene needs the standard leaderboard surface; drive scores through the APJS.Leaderboard component or use APJS.SocialService for custom score/ranking flows rather than legacy SocialKit profile objects. Live data only available after effect publication or in client testing. Has a pre-designed layout with fixed aspect ratio — to resize, use ScreenTransform `scale` with equal X and Y (e.g. {x:0.8, y:0.8}); never use different X/Y scale or modify sizeDelta to change the width/height ratio.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Friends Leaderboard[LeaderBoard]
- **Global Leaderboard**: Global Leaderboard displays the built-in TikTok worldwide ranking UI. Use it when the scene needs the standard leaderboard surface; drive scores through the APJS.Leaderboard component or use APJS.SocialService for custom score/ranking flows rather than legacy SocialKit profile objects. Live data only available after effect publication or in client testing. Has a pre-designed layout with fixed aspect ratio — to resize, use ScreenTransform `scale` with equal X and Y (e.g. {x:0.8, y:0.8}); never use different X/Y scale or modify sizeDelta to change the width/height ratio.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Global Leaderboard[LeaderBoard]
- **Image Picker**: Image Picker allows users to select a photo from their device library and apply it as a texture in the effect. The selected image fills the full frame without transparency.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Image Picker[Image]
- **Image Picker (Background)**: Creates a full-screen 2D backdrop from a photo chosen in the user's photo library, with the main subject auto-cut out so only the surrounding scene remains. Use when you want the photo library picker to fill the frame behind other content.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Image Picker (Background)[Image]
- **Image Picker (Head)**: Image Picker (Head) creates a 2D image from the user's photo library with automatic head cutout — only the face/head is segmented and the rest is made transparent.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Image Picker (Head)[Image]
- **Image Picker (Portrait)**: Image Picker (Portrait) creates a 2D image from the user's photo library with automatic portrait cutout — the shoulders-up portrait is segmented and the background is made transparent.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Image Picker (Portrait)[Image]
- **Image Picker (Subject)**: Image Picker (Subject) creates a 2D image from the user's photo library with automatic subject cutout — the main subject is segmented and the background is made transparent.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Image Picker (Subject)[Image]
- **National Leaderboard**: National Leaderboard displays the built-in TikTok national/country-level ranking UI. Use it when the scene needs the standard leaderboard surface; drive scores through the APJS.Leaderboard component or use APJS.SocialService for custom score/ranking flows rather than legacy SocialKit profile objects. Live data only available after effect publication or in client testing. Has a pre-designed layout with fixed aspect ratio — to resize, use ScreenTransform `scale` with equal X and Y (e.g. {x:0.8, y:0.8}); never use different X/Y scale or modify sizeDelta to change the width/height ratio.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → National Leaderboard[LeaderBoard]
- **Profile Info Animation**: Legacy SocialKit Profile Info Animation object. It displays an animated sequence cycling through multiple friends' profile pictures and usernames. Configurable with sequential or random ordering and adjustable Profile Count (2-30). Use mainly for existing SocialKit/randomizer templates. For new script-controlled friend-avatar features, prefer APJS.SocialService and authored Screen Image slots.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Profile Info Animation[Image]
- **Profile Photo**: Legacy SocialKit Profile Photo object. It displays a TikTok friend's real profile image and auto-creates a 'Username' sibling Image under the same 2D Camera parent. Use it only for compatibility with existing SocialKit templates or when explicitly requested. For new friend-avatar/profile work, prefer APJS.SocialService: create normal Screen Image slots and assign returned UserProfile.profileTexture values in script. Profile Photo preview placeholders can vary by project, and SocialKit is being deprecated.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Profile Photo[Image] + sibling Username[Image]
- **Video Picker**: Video Picker allows users to select a video from their device library and apply it as an animated texture in the effect.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Video Picker[Image]
- **Video Picker (Background)**: Creates a full-screen 2D backdrop from a video chosen in the user's video library, with the main subject auto-cut out so only the surrounding scene remains. Video equivalent of the photo-library backdrop picker.
  - Structure: 2D Camera[Camera] → Video Picker (Background)[Image]
